newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN WOOL PRICES DROP BELOW 700C/KG IN WEEK.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN WOOL PRICES DROP BELOW 700C/KG IN WEEK.

text.p: Australian wool prices fell back at this week's auctions in Sydney and Melbourne, taking the eastern market indicator below 700 cents a kg clean for the first time since late May.
The indicator dropped 22 cents to end at 696 cents a kg.

The relatively high offerings for this time of the season, the holiday period in Europe and an appreciating Australian dollar against European currencies all had a negative impact on the market, the Australian Council of Wool Exporters said.
There was however a noticeable increase in Chinese enquiry at the lower price basis as the week progressed, it said.

Although prices stabilised on the last day of selling, with more widespread competition evident at the lower price basis, the extent of the drop in prices earlier in the week surprised most exporters, the council said in its weekly market review.
A total of 87,841 bales were offered this week with a pass in rate of 16.1 percent, it said.
In its market weekly, Wool International said it sold 575 bales in the week ended August 7 leaving its stockpile of unsold wool at 1,521,593 bales.
In the futures market, a total of 396 lots were traded in the 21 micron contract in the week ended August 7 and open interest increased by 237 contracts to close at 1,353.
The near August contract closed nine cents down at 862 cents a kg clean.
Sales next week are in Sydney, Adelaide and Fremantle with 100,150 bales rostered for sale.
